newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ambassador to Vatican says won't serve again. [CORRECTED 18:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador to Vatican says won't serve again. [CORRECTED 18:56 GMT]

text.p: Family concerns and a desire to return to his home will likely keep sometimes controversial U.S. Ambassador to the Vatican Raymond Flynn from serving a second term if President Bill Clinton is re-elected.
"No, I don't think so," Flynn told Reuters when asked if he would continue in the diplomatic post. "Rome is eternal but Boston is home."

The former Boston mayor, who attended a dinner honouring Ireland's President Mary Robinson on Sunday night, said his wife has stayed in Boston while he has been abroad. His eldest son has had problems with alcohol.
Flynn, who embarrassed Clinton in 1993 by publicly threatening not to take the ambassadorial post, said he is supporting the president's re-election bid.

Flynn's tenure at Vatican City has been marked by controversy involving both his former Boston mayoral campaign organisation and some of his diplomatic practices. Two former Flynn campaign aides were convicted of federal crimes related to campaign funds, while Flynn himself repaid several thousand dollars for illegal expenditures.

Early on the ambassador complained of not being paid enough to keep up expected diplomatic activities and he has been criticised for publicly expressing anti-abortion (corrects by changing from "pro-choice abortion") views while serving as ambassador.
